claims.text: The initial nanoparticles contain five or more metals in equal or near-equal atomic ratios as a homogeneous solid solution.
Retention of single-phase structural and chemical stability is governed primarily by the extent of lattice distortion.
Lattice distortion impedes inter-metal atomic diffusion.
Severe lattice strain creates kinetic barriers to atomic diffusion in high-entropy nanoparticles.
Sluggish atomic diffusion prevents phase segregation and chemical ordering despite high-temperature operation.
Nanoparticles with greater lattice distortion and slower diffusion will retain a homogeneous solid-solution phase with minimal segregation or ordering.
Nanoparticles with lower lattice strain or higher diffusion rates will show more phase separation under otherwise identical operating conditions.
Thermal exposure from 473 to 1923 K can activate diffusion kinetics.
Sufficiently extensive thermal annealing can override the proposed kinetic barriers.
Extreme atmospheres may promote diffusion independently of lattice strain and thereby cause deviations from the prediction.
The proposed relationship is expected to apply within the equal-to-near-equal compositional regime.
Preparation-parameter adjustments can produce nearly composition-matched nanoparticle sets with different degrees of lattice distortion.
